title: Code of Ur-Nammu
summary: The Code of Ur-Nammu, from the Sumerian city of Ur, is the oldest extant law code in the world, dated circa 2100 to 2050 BCE. It was issued under King Ur-Nammu or possibly his son Shulgi and contains 57 laws, most punishing offenses other than capital ones with fines. It later served as a model for codes including Hammurabi's.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia says the dating of circa 2100-2050 BCE is based on middle chronology; short chronology places it circa 2050-2047 BCE. EBSCO gives c. 2112 BCE.

where.historical_name: Ur, Sumerian city on the Euphrates (Third Dynasty of Ur)

importance.justification: World History Encyclopedia calls it the oldest extant law code in the world, predating Hammurabi's by centuries.

related.because: World History Encyclopedia says the code influenced later codes, which in turn served as a model for the Code of Hammurabi.

sources.title: Code of Ur-Nammu: The Oldest Law Code in the World

reviewer_note: Authorship (Ur-Nammu or Shulgi) is reported as uncertain by both sources; dates follow the conventional chronology. Pin is Ur, the king's city (EBSCO gives Ur as locale). Surviving tablets come from other sites; not described here.
